clue.text: Barely sleeps in prison

indicators.note: barely, as if stripped bare, means the word is shorn of its first and last letters

parts.note: slumbers means sleeps

explanation.surface: Someone in jail who can hardly get any rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Prison looks like part of the scene, but it is the definition: LUMBER is old British slang for jail, as in 'in lumber'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumber is a dated British slang word for jail or a pawnshop, so being in lumber means locked up.

clue.text: Upset hermit wiping extremely sore abscess

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
wiping removes, here the outer letters of sore from the hermit

parts.note: a recluse is a hermit

indicators.note: the extremes of sore are its first and last letters

parts.note: its two extreme letters are the ones wiped away

explanation.surface: A distressed hermit cleaning up a very painful abscess.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open sore, close to an abscess as an infected lesion.

clue.text: Club thanks courageous person in fighting unit

parts.note: a bat is a club
ta is British informal for thanks
a lion is a brave person

explanation.surface: Thanking a brave soldier in a military unit with a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is an army unit of several companies.

clue.text: Mature writer supports Republican candidate essentially

indicators.note: in a down answer the writer sits beneath and holds up what comes before
at its essence, the centre of the word, its middle letter

parts.note: the word whose central letter, the fifth of nine, is used
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A seasoned author backing a Republican nominee.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to become mature, as fruit does.

clue.text: Refuse spot introducing comic

indicators.note: the spot word brings in the comic, which ends up sitting inside it

parts.note: to spot is to see
a wag is a joker or comedian

explanation.surface: Apparently someone declines to notice a comedian being brought on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is waste matter carried off in drains, a kind of rubbish.

clue.text: Bears ought to hear us every so often

parts.note: should means ought to

indicators.note: only some letters of the phrase are taken, at regular gaps

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of this phrase are kept

explanation.surface: A demand that the listeners occasionally pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' is a verb (carries, takes on), not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder is to carry or take on a burden, as in bearing responsibility.

clue.text: One visiting made sketches around Rum

indicators.note: the one goes inside, calling on the other word
turned around, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: drew means made sketches

explanation.surface: An artist visiting the Scottish island of Rum to sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is a Hebridean island, but here it is the old British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is British informal for strange or odd, so weird fits.

clue.text: £1.05 adult lost outside food shop; recommendation?

indicators.note: the shortened coin goes round the shop
the adult goes missing from the coin word

parts.note: a guinea was 21 shillings, which is £1.05 in decimal money
a deli or delicatessen

explanation.surface: An adult who lost a pound and a bit outside a food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A guinea was an old British coin worth one pound and one shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A guideline is a piece of advice or general rule on what to do.

clue.text: Means of punishment, once standard, succeeded

parts.note: stock, as in a stock (standard) reply

explanation.surface: Discussion of an old punishment once considered normal and effective.
explanation.definitionFit: The stocks were a wooden frame where offenders were locked by the ankles in public, a historical punishment.

clue.text: Long-faced, a male put down Spare

indicators.note: the letters are dropped, put down and left behind

parts.note: a long face shows someone is unamused
taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for male, taken out alongside the a

explanation.surface: A glum man put down in his spare time.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare and unused both describe something available because it has not been used.

clue.text: Understood revolutionary optimistic attitude is inspiring

indicators.note: turning round, so the run of letters is read from right to left
to inspire is to breathe in, so the phrase holds the letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A sense that a hopeful outlook among rebels is motivating them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied or understood without being stated outright.

clue.text: Supply expert insight

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
vision means foresight or insight

explanation.surface: A specialist providing knowledgeable understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A provision is a stock or store of something, as in provisions of food.

clue.text: Screen clip with ending changed

indicators.note: the final letter of the clip word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: to curtail is to cut short or clip

explanation.surface: Editing a film clip by giving it a different finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' suggests cinema, but it is the definition: something that hides from view.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain is a hanging cloth used to screen a window or stage.

clue.text: They're found on board with snakes, large snakes

definitions.text: They're found on board with snakes

parts.note: adders are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: A description of the board game Snakes and Ladders, with big serpents.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladders share the board with snakes in the children's game Snakes and Ladders.

clue.text: Acts I deny performing for criminal association

indicators.note: the letters act out a new role, rearranged into another word

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone denying that their stage acts are a front for organised crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime syndicate is a group of gangsters organised to run illegal business.

clue.text: Pass over bananas to eat with Nigel shortly

indicators.note: slang for crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder

indicators.note: cut short, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: the name taken as written, before it is cut short

explanation.surface: Instructions to get past bananas by eating them alongside Nigel.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate an obstacle is to get over or past it successfully.

clue.text: Heed command on parade ground?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: notice or careful regard
second meaning: the drill order for soldiers to stand straight

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second definition as an example: the word barked by a sergeant major.
explanation.definitionFit: Attention means notice paid to something and is also the order calling soldiers to stand to.

clue.text: Heard European will stop obscenity returning

indicators.note: the European plugs the word as a stopper does, sitting inside it
coming back, so the word for obscenity is written backwards

parts.note: dirt is smut or obscenity

explanation.surface: A European set to halt a resurgence of smut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' is the definition in its courtroom sense, not a sound clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who has heard a case has tried it in court.

clue.text: Doctor was kept in old TV series

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A doctor who was kept in hospital, as in an old television drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Twin Peaks was David Lynch's cult American mystery drama from the early 1990s.

clue.text: Vehicle, source of woe since new

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is used
ago, as in 'long since' meaning long ago

explanation.surface: A car that has been nothing but trouble since it was bought new.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a wheeled cart or vehicle for carrying goods.

clue.text: Quaint humour shown by posh sleuth reportedly

indicators.note: as reported by word of mouth, so the name is said aloud

parts.note: Lord Peter Wimsey, Dorothy L. Sayers's aristocratic detective

explanation.surface: An aristocratic detective whose quirky wit is on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsy is playful, fanciful or quaint humour.

clue.text: Hardy character tackles points displaying irritation

indicators.note: the character takes the points on, wrapping round them

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
tines are the points of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: A literary heroine taking on sharp prongs and getting cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Testiness is short-tempered irritability, being easily annoyed.

clue.text: Individual record

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a short music release with one main track

explanation.definitionFit: Single means one alone and is also a song released on its own as a record.

clue.text: Current exercise underway

parts.note: in, as in fashionable or current
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: A fitness routine that is currently going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests electricity (I), but here it means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in train is in progress, already set going.

clue.text: Head off, reluctant to concede opponents time

indicators.note: conceding means giving up, so these letters are surrendered

parts.note: averse means unwilling or reluctant
South and East, as rival partnerships at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to give ground to rivals for extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play against East-West, so two compass points can be opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a crisis is to head it off or prevent it happening.

clue.text: Third person keeping fit to become army officer

indicators.note: the person holds the fit word within

parts.note: in Genesis Cain, son of Adam and Eve, is the third person to live
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: Someone working out to qualify for a military commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third person' looks grammatical (he, she, it), but it is Cain, after Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned rank in the army, above lieutenant.

clue.text: Enthusiastic welcome in Switzerland at all times

parts.note: e'er is the poetic short form of ever

explanation.surface: A warm greeting that is always given in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheer is a shout of encouragement or welcome.

clue.text: Element of confusing talk Jack ignored

indicators.note: the jack is left out of the word

parts.note: jargon is technical language that confuses outsiders

explanation.surface: Part of a baffling speech that Jack paid no attention to.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, a chemical element.

clue.text: Son, a bit keen to mix lager with cider

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: these words are taken as written for the fodder

explanation.surface: A son who is rather eager to blend beer and cider.
explanation.walkthrough: A snakebite is a British pub drink of lager and cider in equal measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakebite is the name for a drink of lager mixed half and half with cider.

clue.text: US city loses out finding financial backer

indicators.note: the letters of the word loses are taken out of the city, three from the front and two from the back

parts.note: Los Angeles, in California

explanation.surface: An American city on the slide that goes looking for an investor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' is not a verb here: the letters L-O-S-E-S themselves leave the city, LOS from the front and ES from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a backer who invests money in a theatrical production or new business.

clue.text: Tidy space used by cattle formerly

parts.note: neat is an archaic word for cattle
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A tidy area once grazed by cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten is to make orderly or tidy something up.

clue.text: Revolt of group seizing southern island

indicators.note: the group grabs hold of the other letters, surrounding them

parts.note: a ring is a gang or group

explanation.surface: Rebels taking over an island in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or rebellion against authority.
